LESSON: HOLDING TOOLS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Tools and Production
Topic 4.1: Holding Tools
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Holding Tools, part of Tools and Production in Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are holding tools used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify holding tools used in day-to-day life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Holding Tools in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select holding tools for performing given tasks,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Holding Tools in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use holding tools to perform given tasks,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Holding Tools in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. care for holding tools used in day-to-day life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Holding Tools in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the importance of holding tools in day-to-day life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Holding Tools in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify holding tools used in day-to-day life,

   Holding Tools helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. select holding tools for performing given tasks,

   Holding Tools helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use holding tools to perform given tasks,

   Holding Tools helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. care for holding tools used in day-to-day life,

   Holding Tools helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the importance of holding tools in day-to-day life.

   Holding Tools helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use visual aids or real objects to identify holding tools,

2. choose holding tools for different tasks,

3. discuss uses of different types of holding tools (pliers, clamps, tongs, clips, vice),

4. use print or digital media to search for information on safe use of holding tools,

5. demonstrate safe use of holding tools

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use visual aids or real objects to identify holding tools,
2. choose holding tools for different tasks,
3. discuss uses of different types of holding tools (pliers, clamps, tongs, clips, vice),
4. use print or digital media to search for information on safe use of holding tools,
5. demonstrate safe use of holding tools

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Holding Tools together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: learner develops listening and speaking skills when discussing the uses of different

types of holding tools.

• Learning to Learn: learner reflects on own work when demonstrating safe use of holding tools.

Values:
• Unity: learner cooperates with others when discussing on the safe use of holding tools.

• Responsibility: learner exercises accountability as they clean and safely store holding tools.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Personal Safety and Security: learner demonstrates basic safety skills as they safely use holding tools to perform tasks.

Link to other Subjects:

Agriculture: learner enhances skills on use of farm tools during demonstration on the safe use of holding tools.

Main points to remember:

1. identify holding tools used in day-to-day life,
2. select holding tools for performing given tasks,
3. use holding tools to perform given tasks,
4. care for holding tools used in day-to-day life,
5. appreciate the importance of holding tools in day-to-day life.

Remember the key question: How are holding tools used in day-to-day life?
